environment.description: Kubernetes pod with container spec: securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem=true. No emptyDir, hostPath, or PVC volumes mounted. The container's entire filesystem layer is immutable at the VFS level via the OCI runtime (runc) enforcement of the ro rootfs propagation flag. Note: the application code still attempts os.MkdirAll and os.Symlink calls but these will receive EROFS (read-only file system) from the kernel. The pod also has an annotation 'seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/pod: runtime/default' but this does NOT block symlink(2) — the filesystem immutability alone is what prevents exploitation. There is no writable volume of any kind (no tmpfs, no emptyDir, no PVC). The /tmp directory exists in the image layer but is part of the read-only overlay.

config.notes: No writable filesystem paths available. All overlay layers mounted read-only. /proc and /sys mounted with default container restrictions.
